transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can’t stop thinking about how bad I look, especially my face and stomach, and it’s gotten to where I don’t want people to see me anymore. It’s just really hard to even leave the house because I feel so embarrassed by my appearance.

When you avoid going out, is it mainly because you fear other people will judge or embarrass you in social situations, or is it because you are specifically preoccupied with a perceived flaw in your appearance?

It is definitely because of how I look. I am just so embarrassed by my face looking saggy and blotchy, and how my stomach looks, that I'm convinced people will stare right at those flaws and judge me. I just can't bear the thought of anyone seeing how bad I look now.
Do you spend a lot of time checking, comparing, or trying to hide these specific appearance flaws, or do you mainly avoid people because you fear embarrassment in social situations in general?

I spend so much time checking—I go to the bathroom mirror every half hour to pull at my cheek skin, poke my stomach, and change my shirt multiple times while asking my wife for reassurance. I've started avoiding church, farm meetings, and even my cardiology appointments because I'm just too ashamed of my face and stomach and dread people staring at those specific areas.
Do you believe these appearance flaws are definitely real, or could they possibly be exaggerated by your mind? Have you ever thought that others might see you as normal despite how you feel?

My wife, my daughter, and even my pastor have all tried to reassure me that I look normal and they don't see what I'm talking about. But when I look in the mirror, these flaws feel completely real and terrible, and I can't help but feel like everyone else will stare and judge me. It just feels so obvious to me.
When you avoid people, is it mainly because you fear being judged in social situations in general, or is it specifically because you are focused on these perceived flaws in your face and stomach?

It is strictly because of how I look, not because I have a general fear of socializing. I actually used to love going to church, playing guitar, and attending farm meetings, but now I avoid them because I'm convinced people will stare at my saggy, blotchy face and my stomach.
Do you ever think there might be a chance that your appearance concerns are being exaggerated by your mind, or are you completely certain that your face and stomach really look this bad to others?

I am completely certain that they really do look that bad. My family and pastor try to reassure me, but I think they're just trying to spare my feelings. To me, the sagging in my face and my stomach are completely real, and I'm convinced everyone else will see them immediately.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs, such as thinking someone is trying to harm you, watch you, or send you special messages, or is the concern only about your appearance?

No, I don't have any thoughts like that about people trying to harm me, spy on me, or send me messages. My worries are entirely focused on how bad my face and stomach look, and the fear that everyone is staring at and judging my appearance.
Have you ever noticed anything about your appearance that seems clearly untrue or impossible to other people, or has this always felt completely real and unquestionable to you?

It has always felt completely real and unquestionable to me. Even though my wife, family, and pastor keep telling me that nothing about my appearance has changed and they can't see what I'm talking about, I remain absolutely convinced the flaws are there. When I look in the mirror, it is just too obvious, and I'm certain that others will stare at them.
Have you ever been able to question this belief at all, or is it completely fixed and impossible for you to doubt even a little?

I'm not really sure how to answer if it's completely fixed, but it just feels incredibly real and hard to ignore. The thoughts and feelings are just so overwhelming that it's difficult to even think about doubting them.
Do you ever have any doubt that these flaws might be exaggerated by your mind, or are you completely convinced they are truly there and obvious to other people?

I don't have any doubts; I am completely convinced these flaws are real and highly visible. Even though my wife and pastor tell me they don't see anything, I just know people at church and the clinic are staring right at my saggy face and stomach. It feels far too obvious to just be something my mind is exaggerating.
Besides the appearance concern, have you ever had other fixed beliefs that seem clearly untrue to others, such as being watched, followed, harmed, or receiving special messages?
No, I have never had any of those kinds of thoughts or feelings. My worries are strictly limited to how I look, especially my face and my stomach.
Have you ever heard, seen, or felt things that other people do not, or had any experiences that made you think something unusual was happening beyond the appearance concerns?

No, I have never heard, seen, or felt things that aren't really there, and nothing unusual like that has ever happened to me. My mind is entirely focused on my appearance concerns and how bad my face and stomach look.

Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that other people would consider clearly untrue, such as being watched, followed, harmed, or given special messages? Or is the concern only about your appearance?

No, I have never believed anything like that. My concern is strictly about my appearance, especially my face and my stomach, and how embarrassing it is for me to be seen. I only worry about people judging how I look.

Have you ever had any time when you could recognize that these appearance concerns might be exaggerated or not actually true, even a little? Or have you always been completely certain that the flaws are real and obvious to others?

It is hard to say if I've ever really doubted it, but most of the time it feels completely real to me despite what my family says. When I look in the mirror, it is just too hard to believe that those flaws aren't actually there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with hypochondriacal/health-related somatic preoccupation in ICD-10 candidate terms, but the interview actually shows a fixed preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (face and stomach), repetitive checking/reassurance seeking, marked avoidance, and near-delusional conviction without hallucinations or other psychotic symptoms. The main differential is social phobia due to avoidance of church/meetings, but the avoidance is explicitly driven by appearance concerns rather than fear of social scrutiny in general. Delusional disorder is less likely because the belief is circumscribed to appearance and there are no other psychotic features.
